Question: If \(p,\) \(q,\) and \(M\) are positive numbers and \(q\lt100,\) then the number obtained by increasing \(M\) by \(p\%\) and decreasing the result by \(q\%\) exceeds \(M\) if and only if
Solution:
The decrease is a percentage of the enlarged amount, so the two changes must be applied successively. Increasing by \(p\%\) multiplies by \(1+p/100\), and decreasing by \(q\%\) multiplies by \(1-q/100\). The final amount is therefore
\[
M\left(1+\frac p{100}\right)\left(1-\frac q{100}\right).
\]
Because \(M>0\), this exceeds \(M\) exactly when
\[
\begin{aligned}
(100+p)(100-q)&>10000,\\
p(100-q)&>100q.
\end{aligned}
\]
The condition \(q<100\) ensures that \(100-q>0\), so division preserves the inequality and gives
\[
p>\frac{100q}{100-q}.
\]
Every step is reversible. At equality the final amount equals \(M\), so the required condition is the strict inequality in choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
